doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Lester Bowie's Brass Fantasy and 'Avant Pop'
summary: Stewart became the bass player in Bowie's Brass Fantasy; Rowe questions the intent of the record 'Avant Pop'.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So you’ve gone from music that has a long history of a tradition and stuff that’s pretty groundbreaking too. Is that fair to say?

Oh yeah sure. Well he, again, because he had heard me play with Arthur Blythe and so he invited me to be a part of Brass Fantasy, and so I got to be the bass player in that group of all brass players. Again, homage and tribute to New Orleans while again taking the music and trying to go to the next mile while using traditional instrumentation, you just are paying homage to the tradition and not necessarily being traditional. You know? And he took it to a whole bunch of other different places.
When I was listening to — the one I have is called “Avante Pop.”
And as I was listening to it, sometimes you’re trying to figure out what is the intention of this record. And sometimes I almost felt like he was trying to get airplay on an easy
listening station — or maybe not easy listening but he’s doing “Saving All My Love for You” but then on the other side of the record there’s this thing called “No Shit.”
And so okay, now where’s he going with this.
